documentation_shape: The held record names only the qualifying income-source categories as evidence: a foreign-employer relationship, freelance-client contracts, or a foreign-registered online business — mirroring Colombia's active-income-only framing. No specific document checklist (bank-statement look-back period, apostille/legalization standard, health-insurance minimum, or criminal-record requirement) was found in available sources for this specific route, in contrast to Rentista's and Pensionado's own documented standards (12+ months of bank statements, mandatory $20,000 health coverage, government/employer pension certification). This asymmetry looks like a genuine gap in what's publicly documented about Digital Nomad's own paperwork, not a confirmed absence of requirements — a one-cycle 360-day category almost certainly has its own consular checklist, but it is not established in available sources.

A certification from the paying government, international organization, or private company, confirming the pension is paid on a regular and permanent basis for services rendered abroad; legalized via Argentine consulate or apostille if the issuing country is a Hague Convention signatory; translated into Spanish by a certified public translator if not already in Spanish — the same foreign-document legalization discipline other Argentine residency routes carry. Mandatory private health insurance with a minimum $20,000 in coverage applies to Argentine temporary residents generally as of Decreto 366/2025 (July 2025), since public healthcare access was stripped from this status — documented specifically for Rentista's own process rather than independently confirmed for Pensionado, but the same decree and residency category apply to both.

Real client-experience-level sourcing (not the headline government description) describes document-heavy scrutiny: 12+ months of consistent bank statements as the practical evidentiary standard, near-automatic requests for further supporting documentation beyond the initial filing, document prep/apostille/translation adding 4-8 weeks before the official processing clock even starts, and — a genuinely new hard requirement since Decreto 366/2025 (effective July 2025) stripped temporary residents of public healthcare access — mandatory private health insurance with a minimum $20,000 in coverage. Real total cost reported at USD $5,000-7,000 per single applicant, well above the headline consular-fee figure.

documentation_shape: Bank statements demonstrating the required foreign income received over the prior year (a higher flat bar applies with dependents), proof the income is stable and foreign-sourced, proof of NO Guatemalan income and no employment relationship with any Guatemalan entity, and international health insurance. No Guatemalan guarantor is required — a friction point older categories had. Since 2026, Guatemala's immigration authority (IGM) also conducts a mandatory field visit to verify the applicant's actual address as part of processing.

Documented proof of the qualifying investment, verifiable and shown to have arrived from abroad by bank transfer. Most commonly real estate: a notarized public deed (escritura pública) registered in the national property registry (Registro General de la Propiedad) — unregistered property does not count, and multiple properly-documented properties can be combined to reach the bar. Business capital, an earmarked bank deposit, or purchase of an existing business also qualify. Processing includes a mandatory field-verification step in which an inspector from Guatemala's immigration authority (IGM) confirms the investment and the applicant's address actually exist; realistic notarial/legal assistance costs sit on top of the official fees.

An apostilled criminal background check issued within the last 2 years (a 2025 easing — previously 5), proof of the qualifying passive income (pension, rental income, investment income, or dividends; US Social Security is among the most commonly accepted sources), and standard biographical documents. Filing is in person at the foreigners' office (Subdirección de Extranjería) of Guatemala's immigration authority (IGM) in Guatemala City, and every apostille is far easier obtained in the home country before traveling. Once granted, the income must be re-proven every 5 years.

documentation_shape: For Portugal's passive-income residency visa (D7): a savings floor of at least €11,040 (12x the €920/month income threshold), plus 50% for a spouse and 30% per dependent child, mirroring the income threshold's own family add-ons. For pension income specifically (one of D7's three named legal applicant categories, per gov.pt), the documentary standard under Portaria n.º 1563/2007 (as amended by Portaria n.º 760/2009) is a certificate issued by the official entity of the country granting the pension, with an authenticated declaration — a distinct, named standard, cross-corroborated across multiple 2026 practitioner guides, though the Portaria's own full primary text has not been directly verified from source. For ordinary (non-pension) passive income — rental, dividends/investment, IP royalties — no equivalently specific document-format standard (bank-statement look-back period, notarization requirement) was found in available sources beyond the general income-source list itself. Applicants also face Portugal's immigration and asylum agency (AIMA)'s own document-rejection-strict processing environment generally (since April 28, 2025, AIMA rejects any application missing even one required document immediately rather than allowing supplementation) — a process-wide fact, not D7-specific, but directly relevant to how much documentation slack an applicant actually has.

documentation_shape: Savings floor: at least €11,040 (12x D7's own €920/month threshold, since D8's savings requirement is stated as the same figure with the same dependent add-ons), plus the same 50%/30% dependent add-ons. Process-specific wrinkles worth carrying alongside the document list itself: the visa must be secured through a consulate before arrival (the 'Manifestation of Interest' in-country application loophole is now closed), and D8 processing specifically is taking 6-9 months as of June 2026, driven by backlog at Portugal's immigration and asylum agency (AIMA) — both real, dated, and D8-specific rather than general Portugal-wide facts.

documentation_shape: A bank balance of 500,000 THB held for at least 3 months before applying — cryptocurrency and investment-portfolio balances are explicitly not accepted — plus a clean immigration record, and the application must be filed from outside Thailand on the official e-Visa platform (which reportedly checks IP address and GPS data to enforce that rule). Passive income alone (investment, dividend, savings-drawdown) is explicitly described as insufficient as primary proof — it can supplement active-income documentation but cannot substitute for it.

Ordinary pension/retirement/investment income is the accepted evidence class — no active-employment documentation standard exists on this route. This tier additionally carries its own 14-country eligible-nationality list, gated separately — see TH:o-x-nationality-restriction.

income_threshold: None — one-time cash payment only, no ongoing income/asset test
accepts_passive_income: N/A — no income or asset test of any kind, active or passive
documentation_shape: A one-time membership payment for the chosen tier is the entire financial qualification — no income proof, no asset proof, no ongoing financial test of any kind, active or passive. The documentation burden is essentially the purchase itself, which is why this is the one Thai route where the income-type question does not arise at all.

threshold_label: Temporary Residence Card (TRC) via Registered Investment — capital threshold
unit: USD, lump-sum registered-investment capital, roughly (VND 3,000,000,000 — the ĐT3-tier floor — converted at ~26,200 VND/USD, 2026-08-09)
documentation_shape: ĐT1 ≥VND100bn (~$3.8M): visa up to 5yr, Temporary Residence Card (TRC) up to 10yr. ĐT2 VND50-<100bn (~$1.9-3.8M): visa up to 5yr, TRC up to 5yr (one source: 10yr). ĐT3 VND3-<50bn (~$114.5k-1.9M): visa up to 3yr, TRC up to 2-3yr (one source: 10yr — sources disagree on ĐT3's TRC ceiling specifically). ĐT4 <VND3bn (~<$114.5k): visa only, up to 12 months, no TRC.

converts_to_pr: Yes (conditional on the ZAR 37,000/month income being guaranteed for the applicant's lifetime — a lifelong state pension or irrevocable annuity specifically, per Immigration Act Section 27(e); an ordinary non-lifelong passive-income proof doesn't clear this specific gate even if it clears the visa's own income test)
accepts_passive_income: Yes (rental income, dividends, and interest from investments are all explicitly confirmed acceptable, combinable with each other and with pension payments — not limited to a formal pension/annuity instrument)
